[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

- **[[293]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-293 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  this section,

  [[custodian]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[custodian]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person in whose custody
      a package is placed under subsection
      (3); ([gardien]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[judge]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[judge]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a judge of a superior court
      having jurisdiction in the province where the matter arises or a
      judge of the Federal Court; ([juge]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[lawyer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[lawyer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means, in the Province of Quebec,
      an advocate, lawyer or notary and, in any other province, a
      barrister or solicitor; ([avocat]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[officer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person acting under the
      authority conferred by any of sections 276 and 288 to
      291; ([fonctionnaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[solicitor-client privilege]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[solicitor-client privilege]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
      right, if any, that a person has in a superior court in the
      province where the matter arises to refuse to disclose an oral or
      documentary communication on the ground that the communication is
      one passing between the person and the person's lawyer in
      professional confidence, except that, for the purposes of this
      section, an accounting record of a lawyer, including any
      supporting invoice, voucher or cheque, shall be deemed not to be
      such a communication. ([privilège des communications entre client
      et avocat]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Solicitor-client privilege defence

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a lawyer is prosecuted for failure to comply
  with a requirement under section 289 with respect to information or a
  document, the lawyer shall be acquitted if the lawyer establishes to
  the satisfaction of the court that the lawyer

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} believed on reasonable grounds that a client of the
    lawyer had a solicitor-client privilege in respect of the
    information or document; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} communicated to the Minister, or to a person duly
    authorized to act for the Minister, the lawyer's refusal to comply
    with the requirement, together with a claim that a named client of
    the lawyer had a solicitor-client privilege in respect of the
    information or document.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Seizure where privilege claimed

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where, under section 290, an officer is about to
  seize a document in the possession of a lawyer and the lawyer claims
  that a named client of the lawyer has a solicitor-client privilege in
  respect of the document, the officer shall, without inspecting,
  examining or making copies of the document,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} seize the document and place it, together with any
    other document in respect of which the lawyer at the same time makes
    the same claim on behalf of the same client, in a package and
    suitably seal and identify the package; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} place the package in the custody of the sheriff of
    the district or county in which the seizure was made or, if the
    officer and the lawyer agree in writing on a person to act as
    custodian, in the custody of that person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Retention where privilege claimed

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If, under section 288, an officer is about to inspect
  or examine a document in the possession of a lawyer or if, under
  section 289, the Minister has required the provision of a document by
  a lawyer, and the lawyer claims that a named client of the lawyer has
  a solicitor-client privilege in respect of the document, no officer
  shall inspect or examine the document and the lawyer shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} place the document, together with any other
    document in respect of which the lawyer at the same time makes the
    same claim on behalf of the same client, in a package and suitably
    seal and identify the package or, if the officer and the lawyer
    agree, allow the pages of the document to be initialed and numbered
    or otherwise suitably identified; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} retain it and ensure that it is preserved until it
    is produced to a judge as required under this section and an order
    is issued under this section in respect of the document.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application to judge

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where a document is seized and placed in custody
  under subsection (3) or is retained under subsection (4), the client,
  or the lawyer on behalf of the client, may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} within fourteen days after the day the document was
    so placed in custody or began to be so retained apply, on three
    clear days notice of motion to the Deputy Attorney General of
    Canada, to a judge for an order

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} fixing a day, not later than twenty-one days
      after the date of the order, and a place for the determination of
      the question whether the client has a solicitor-client privilege
      in respect of the document, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} requiring the production of the document to the
      judge at that time and place;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} serve a copy of the order on the Deputy Attorney
    General of Canada and, where applicable, on the custodian within six
    days after the day it was made and, within the same time, pay to the
    custodian the estimated expenses of transporting the document to and
    from the place of hearing and of safeguarding it; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the client or lawyer has proceeded as authorized
    by paragraph (b), apply at the appointed time and place for an order
    determining the question.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposition of application

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} An application made under paragraph (5)(c) shall be
  heard [in camera]{.otherLang lang="la"} and, on the application, the
  judge

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} may, if the judge considers it necessary to
    determine the question, inspect the document and, if the judge does
    so, the judge shall ensure that it is repackaged and resealed; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} shall decide the matter summarily, and if the judge
    is of the opinion that the client

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} has a solicitor-client privilege in respect of
      the document, the judge shall order the release of the document to
      the lawyer, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} does not have a solicitor-client privilege in
      respect of the document, the judge shall order that

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the custodian deliver the document to the
        officer or some other person designated by the Commissioner in
        the case of a document that was seized and placed in custody
        under subsection (3), or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the lawyer make the document available for
        inspection or examination by the officer or other person
        designated by the Commissioner in the case of a document that
        was retained under subsection (4),

      and shall, at the same time, deliver concise reasons in which the
      document shall be identified without divulging any of its details.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Order on application

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} Where a document is seized and placed in custody
  under subsection (3) or is retained under subsection (4) and a judge,
  on the application of the Attorney General of Canada, is satisfied
  that neither the client nor the lawyer has made an application under
  paragraph (5)(a) or, having made such an application, that neither the
  client nor the lawyer has made an application under paragraph (5)(c),
  the judge shall order that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the custodian deliver the document to the officer
    or some other person designated by the Commissioner in the case of a
    document that was seized and placed in custody under subsection (3);
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the lawyer make the document available for
    inspection or examination by the officer or other person designated
    by the Commissioner in the case of a document that was retained
    under subsection (4).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Delivery by custodian

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} The custodian shall deliver the document

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to the lawyer

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with a consent executed by the
      officer or by or on behalf of the Deputy Attorney General of
      Canada or the Commissioner, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with an order of a judge under
      this section; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} to the officer or some other person designated by
    the Commissioner

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with a consent executed by the
      lawyer or the client, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with an order of a judge under
      this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Continuation by another judge

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} Where the judge to whom an application is made under
  paragraph (5)(a) cannot for any reason act or continue to act in the
  application under paragraph (5)(c), the application under paragraph
  (5)(c) may be made to another judge.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Costs

  [(10)]{.lawlabel} No costs may be awarded on the disposition of any
  application under this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Directions

  [(11)]{.lawlabel} Where any question arises as to the course to be
  followed in connection with anything done or being done under this
  section, other than subsection (2), (3) or (4), and there is no
  direction in this section with respect thereto, a judge may give such
  direction with regard thereto as, in the judge's opinion, is most
  likely to carry out the object of this section of allowing
  solicitor-client privilege for proper purposes.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Prohibition

  [(12)]{.lawlabel} The custodian shall not deliver a document to any
  person except in accordance with an order of a judge or a consent
  under this section or except to any officer or servant of the
  custodian for the purposes of safeguarding the document.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(13)]{.lawlabel} No officer shall inspect, examine or seize a
  document in the possession of a lawyer without giving the lawyer a
  reasonable opportunity to make a claim under this section.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Copies

  [(14)]{.lawlabel} At any time while a document is in the custody of a
  custodian under this section, a judge may, on [ex parte]{.otherLang
  lang="la"} application of the lawyer, by order, authorize the lawyer
  to examine or make a copy of the document in the presence of the
  custodian or the judge, which order shall contain such provisions as
  may be necessary to ensure that the document is repackaged and that
  the package is resealed without alteration or damage.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Waiver of privilege

  [(15)]{.lawlabel} Where, for the purpose of subsection (2), (3) or
  (4), a lawyer makes a claim that a named client of the lawyer has a
  solicitor-client privilege in respect of information or a document,
  the lawyer shall at the same time communicate to the Minister or to a
  person duly authorized to act for the Minister the address of the
  client last known to the lawyer so that the Minister may endeavour to
  advise the client of the claim of privilege that has been made on the
  client's behalf and thereby give the client an opportunity, if it is
  practicable within the time limited by this section, to waive the
  claim of privilege before the matter is to be decided by a judge or
  other tribunal.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Compliance

  [(16)]{.lawlabel} No person shall hinder, molest or interfere with any
  person doing anything that the person is authorized to do under this
  section or prevent or attempt to prevent any person doing any such
  thing and, notwithstanding any other Act or law, every person shall,
  unless the person is unable to do so, do everything the person is
  required to do under this section.

- \[NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated
  text
- see relevant amending Acts and regulations.\]
- 1990, c. 45, s. 12
- 1999, c. 17, s. 155
- 2000, c. 30, s. 88
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Information respecting non-resident
persons

**[[294]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-294 .sectionLabel}** Every corporation that,
at any time in a taxation year, was resident in Canada or carried on
business or a commercial activity in Canada shall, in respect of each
non-resident person with whom it was not dealing at arm's length at any
time in the year, file with the Minister, within six months after the
end of the year, prescribed information for the year in respect of
transactions with that person.

::: HistoricalNote
- \[NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated
  text
- see relevant amending Acts and regulations.\]
- 1990, c. 45, s. 12
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Definitions

- **[[295]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-295 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In
  this section,

  [[aboriginal government]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[aboriginal government]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an aboriginal
      government as defined in subsection 2(1) of the
      [Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements
      Act](/eng/acts/F-7.8); ([gouvernement autochtone]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[authorized person]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[authorized person]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person who is
      engaged or employed, or who was formerly engaged or employed, by
      or on behalf of Her Majesty in right of Canada to assist in
      carrying out the provisions of this Act; ([personne
      autorisée]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[business number]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[business number]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the number (other
      than a Social Insurance Number) used by the Minister to identify

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a registrant for the purposes of this Part,

      - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} a person registered under Subdivision E of
        Division II, or

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an applicant (other than an individual) for a
        rebate under this Part; ([numéro d'entreprise]{.DefinedTermLink
        lang="fr"})

  [[confidential information]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[confidential information]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means information
      of any kind and in any form that relates to one or more persons
      and that is

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} obtained by or on behalf of the Minister for
        the purposes of this Part, or

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} prepared from information referred to in
        paragraph (a),

      but does not include information that does not directly or
      indirectly reveal the identity of the person to whom it relates
      and, for the purposes of applying subsections (3), (6) and (7) to
      a representative of a government entity who is not an official,
      includes only the information described in paragraph
      (5)(j); ([renseignement confidentiel]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[contact information]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[contact information]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in respect of a
      holder of a business number, means the name, address, telephone
      number, facsimile number and preferred language of communication
      of the holder, or similar information as specified by the Minister
      in respect of the holder, and includes such information in respect
      of one or more

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} trustees of the holder, if the holder is a
        trust,

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} members of the holder, if the holder is a
        partnership,

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} officers of the holder, if the holder is a
        corporation, or

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} officers or members of the holder, in any other
        case; ([coordonnées]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[corporate information]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[corporate information]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in respect of a
      holder of a business number that is a corporation, means the name
      (including the number assigned by the incorporating authority),
      date of incorporation, jurisdiction of incorporation and any
      information on the dissolution, reorganization, amalgamation,
      winding-up or revival of the corporation; ([renseignements
      d'entreprise]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[court of appeal]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[court of appeal]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the meaning assigned
      by the definition of that expression in section 2 of the [Criminal
      Code](/eng/acts/C-46); ([cour d'appel]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[government entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[government entity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a department or agency of the government of
        Canada or of a province,

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a municipality,

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an aboriginal government,

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a corporation all of the shares (except
        directors' qualifying shares) of the capital stock of which are
        owned by one or more persons each of which is

        - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Her Majesty in right of Canada,

        - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} Her Majesty in right of a province,

        - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a municipality, or

        - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a corporation described in this paragraph,
          or

      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a board or commission, established by Her
        Majesty in right of Canada or Her Majesty in right of a
        province, that performs an administrative or regulatory function
        of government, or by a municipality, that performs an
        administrative or regulatory function of a
        municipality; ([entité gouvernementale]{.DefinedTermLink
        lang="fr"})

  [[municipality]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[municipality]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} does not include a local
      authority determined by the Minister to be a municipality under
      paragraph (b) of the definition
      [[municipality]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in subsection
      123(1); ([municipalité]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[official]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[official]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person who is employed in
      the service of, who occupies a position of responsibility in the
      service of, or who is engaged by or on behalf of, Her Majesty in
      right of Canada or a province, or a person who was formerly so
      employed, who formerly occupied such a position or who formerly
      was so engaged; ([fonctionnaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[registration information]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[registration information]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in respect of a
      holder of a business number, means

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any information pertaining to the legal form of
        the holder,

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the type of activities carried on or proposed
        to be carried on by the holder,

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} each date on which

        - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the business number was issued to the holder,

        - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the holder began activities,

        - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the holder ceased or resumed activities, or

        - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the business number assigned to the holder
          was changed, and

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the reasons for the cessation, resumption or
        change referred to in subparagraph (c)(iii) or
        (iv); ([renseignements relatifs à
        l'inscription]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[representative]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[representative]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} of a government entity
      means a person who is employed in the service of, who occupies a
      position of responsibility in the service of, or who is engaged by
      or on behalf of, a government entity, and includes, for the
      purposes of subsections (2), (3), (6) and (7), a person who was
      formerly so employed, who formerly occupied such a position or who
      formerly was so engaged. ([représentant]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Provision of information

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Except as authorized under this section, no official
  or other representative of a government entity shall knowingly

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide, or allow to be provided, to any person any
    confidential information;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} allow any person to have access to any confidential
    information; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} use any confidential information other than in the
    course of the administration or enforcement of this Part.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Evidence relating to confidential
  information

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite any other Act of Parliament or other law, no
  official or other representative of a government entity shall be
  required, in connection with any legal proceedings, to give or produce
  evidence relating to any confidential information.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Communications where proceedings have
  been commenced

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (2) and (3) do not apply in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} criminal proceedings, either by indictment or on
    summary conviction, that have been commenced by the laying of an
    information or the preferring of an indictment, under an Act of
    Parliament; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any legal proceedings relating to the
    administration or enforcement of this Act, the [Canada Pension
    Plan](/eng/acts/C-8), the Employment Insurance Act, the Unemployment
    Insurance Act or any other Act of Parliament or law of a province
    that provides for the imposition of a tax or duty.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Circumstances involving danger

  [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may provide to appropriate persons any
  confidential information relating to imminent danger of death or
  physical injury to any individual.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure of personal information

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} An official may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide such confidential information to any person
    as may reasonably be regarded as necessary for the purpose of the
    administration or enforcement of this Act, solely for that purpose;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide to a person confidential information that
    can reasonably be regarded as necessary for the purposes of
    determining any liability or obligation of the person or any refund,
    rebate or input tax credit to which the person is or may become
    entitled under this Act;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} provide, allow to be provided, or allow inspection
    of or access to any confidential information to or by

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} any person, or any person within a class of
      persons, that the Minister may authorize, subject to such
      conditions as the Minister may specify, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any person otherwise legally entitled thereto by
      reason of an Act of Parliament, solely for the purposes for which
      that person is entitled to the information;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} provide confidential information

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} to an official of the Department of Finance
      solely for the purposes of

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the formulation or evaluation of fiscal policy,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} an administration agreement, as defined in
        subsection 2(1) of the [Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements
        Act](/eng/acts/F-7.8), entered into with an aboriginal
        government, or

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} an administration agreement, as defined in
        subsection 2(1) of the [First Nations Goods and Services Tax
        Act](/eng/acts/F-11.7),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} to an official solely for the purpose of the
      initial implementation of a fiscal policy or for the purposes of
      the administration or enforcement of the [Canada Pension
      Plan](/eng/acts/C-8), the [Employment Insurance
      Act](/eng/acts/E-5.6), the Unemployment Insurance Act or an Act of
      Parliament that provides for the imposition or collection of a tax
      or duty or that provides that displays or indications of the price
      or consideration for property or services include tax under this
      Act,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} to an official solely for the purposes of the
      administration or enforcement of a law of a province that provides
      for the imposition or collection of a tax or duty, that provides
      that displays or indications of the price or consideration for
      property or services include tax under this Act or that provides
      for reimbursements to persons of amounts paid or payable by the
      persons as or on account of tax under this Act,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} to an official of the government of a province
      solely for the purposes of the formulation or evaluation of fiscal
      policy,

    - [(iv.1)]{.lawlabel} to a person authorized by the council of a
      band listed in the schedule to the [Budget Implementation Act,
      2000](/eng/acts/B-9.84) solely for the purposes of the
      formulation, evaluation or initial implementation of fiscal policy
      relating to a tax that the council of the band may impose under a
      by-law made under subsection 24(1) of that Act,

    - [(iv.2)]{.lawlabel} to a person authorized by the governing body
      of a first nation listed in the schedule to the [First Nations
      Goods and Services Tax Act](/eng/acts/F-11.7) solely for the
      purposes of the formulation, evaluation or initial implementation
      of fiscal policy relating to a tax referred to in that Act,

    - [(iv.3)]{.lawlabel} to an official solely for the purpose of the
      administration or enforcement of the [Canada Education Savings
      Act](/eng/acts/C-3.6) or a [[designated provincial
      program]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, as defined in subsection 146.1(1)
      of the [Income Tax Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3),

    - [(iv.4)]{.lawlabel} to an official solely for the purpose of the
      administration or enforcement of the [Canada Disability Savings
      Act](/eng/acts/C-3.5) or a [[designated provincial
      program]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, as defined in subsection 146.4(1)
      of the [Income Tax Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3),

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} to an official of a department or agency of the
      Government of Canada or of a province as to the name, address,
      telephone number, occupation, size or type of business of a
      person, solely for the purposes of enabling that department or
      agency to obtain statistical data for research and analysis,

    - [(v.1)]{.lawlabel} to an official of the Department of Employment
      and Social Development solely for the purpose of the
      administration or enforcement of a program established under the
      authority of the [Department of Employment and Social Development
      Act](/eng/acts/H-5.7) in respect of children who are deceased or
      missing as a result of an offence, or a probable offence, under
      the [Criminal Code](/eng/acts/C-46),

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} to an official solely for the purposes of
      setting off, against any sum of money that may be due or payable
      by Her Majesty in right of Canada, a debt due to

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} Her Majesty in right of Canada, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} Her Majesty in right of a province on account
        of taxes payable to the province where an agreement exists
        between Canada and the province under which Canada is authorized
        to collect taxes on behalf of the province,

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} to an official solely for the purposes of
      section 7.1 of the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements and
      Federal Post-secondary Education and Health Contributions Act,

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} to an official of the Financial Transactions
      and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada solely for the purpose of
      enabling the Centre to evaluate the usefulness of information
      provided by the Centre to the Canada Revenue Agency under the
      [Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing
      Act](/eng/acts/P-24.501),

    - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} to an official of the Canada Revenue Agency
      solely for the purpose of the collection of amounts owing to Her
      Majesty in right of Canada or of a province under the [Government
      Employees Compensation Act](/eng/acts/G-5), the [Canada Labour
      Code](/eng/acts/L-2), the [Merchant Seamen Compensation
      Act](/eng/acts/M-6), the [Canada Student Loans
      Act](/eng/acts/S-23), the [Canada Student Financial Assistance
      Act](/eng/acts/S-22.7), the [Postal Services Continuation Act,
      1997](/eng/acts/P-15.8), the [Wage Earner Protection Program
      Act](/eng/acts/W-0.8), the [Apprentice Loans
      Act](/eng/acts/A-11.9) or a law of a province governing the
      granting of financial assistance to students at the post-secondary
      school level,

    - [(x)]{.lawlabel} to an official of the Canada Revenue Agency
      solely for the purpose of the collection of amounts owing to Her
      Majesty in right of Canada under the Canada Emergency Business
      Account program established by Export Development Canada in
      accordance with an authorization made under subsection 23(1) of
      the [Export Development Act](/eng/acts/E-20),

    - [(xi)]{.lawlabel} to an official of

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the Canada Revenue Agency solely for the
        purposes of the administration or enforcement of the [Dental
        Benefit Act](/eng/acts/D-1.55), or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the Department of Health solely for the
        purposes of the formulation or evaluation of policy for that
        Act,

    - [(xi.1)]{.lawlabel} to an official of

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the Department of Employment and Social
        Development, the Department of Health or the Department of
        Public Works and Government Services, solely for the purpose of
        the administration or enforcement of the Canadian Dental Care
        Plan established under the authority of the [Department of
        Health Act](/eng/acts/H-3.2) in respect of dental service for
        individuals, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the Department of Health solely for the purpose
        of the formulation or evaluation of policy for that plan,

    - [(xii)]{.lawlabel} to an official of the Canada Revenue Agency
      solely for the purposes of the administration or enforcement of
      the [Rental Housing Benefit Act](/eng/acts/R-5.44),

    - [(xiii)]{.lawlabel} to a person who is employed in the service of,
      who occupies a position of responsibility in the service of, or
      who is engaged by or on behalf of, the Canada Mortgage and Housing
      Corporation, solely for the purposes of the formulation or
      evaluation of policy for the [Rental Housing Benefit
      Act](/eng/acts/R-5.44), or

    - [(xiv)]{.lawlabel} to an official solely for the purposes of a
      security review under subsection 83.032(10) or section 83.034 of
      the [Criminal Code](/eng/acts/C-46), if the information can
      reasonably be considered to be relevant to the security review;

  - [(d.1)]{.lawlabel} provide confidential information, or allow the
    inspection of or access to confidential information, as the case may
    be, under, and solely for the purpose of,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 33.1(a) of the [Old Age Security
      Act](/eng/acts/O-9),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an order made under subsection 462.48(3) of the
      [Criminal Code](/eng/acts/C-46), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an order made under the [Mutual Legal
      Assistance in Criminal Matters Act](/eng/acts/M-13.6) to gather or
      send information, for the purposes of an investigation or
      prosecution relating to an act or omission that, if it had
      occurred in Canada, would constitute an offence for which an order
      could be obtained under subsection 462.48(3) of the [Criminal
      Code](/eng/acts/C-46), in response to a request made pursuant to

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} an administrative arrangement entered into
        under section 6 of the [Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal
        Matters Act](/eng/acts/M-13.6), or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} a bilateral agreement for mutual legal
        assistance in criminal matters to which Canada is a party;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} provide confidential information solely for the
    purposes of sections 23 to 25 of the [Financial Administration
    Act](/eng/acts/F-11);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} use confidential information to compile information
    in a form that does not directly or indirectly reveal the identity
    of the person to whom the information relates;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} use, or provide to any person, confidential
    information solely for a purpose relating to the supervision,
    evaluation or discipline of an authorized person by Her Majesty in
    right of Canada in respect of a period during which the authorized
    person was employed by or engaged by or on behalf of Her Majesty in
    right of Canada to assist in the administration or enforcement of
    this Act, to the extent that the information is relevant for that
    purpose;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} provide access to records of confidential
    information to the Librarian and Archivist of Canada or a person
    acting on behalf of or under the direction of the Librarian and
    Archivist, solely for the purposes of section 12 of the [Library and
    Archives of Canada Act](/eng/acts/L-7.7), and transfer such records
    to the care and control of such persons solely for the purposes of
    section 13 of that Act;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} use confidential information relating to a person
    to provide information to that person;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (5.01), provide to a
    representative of a government entity the business number of, the
    name of (including any trade name or other name used by), and any
    contact information, corporate information and registration
    information in respect of, the holder of a business number, if the
    information is provided solely for the purpose of the administration
    or enforcement of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an Act of Parliament or of a legislature of a
      province, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a by-law of a municipality or a law of an
      aboriginal government;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} provide confidential information to any person,
    solely for the purposes of the administration or enforcement of a
    law of a province that provides for workers' compensation benefits;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} provide confidential information to a police
    officer (within the meaning assigned by subsection 462.48(17) of the
    [Criminal Code](/eng/acts/C-46)) solely for the purpose of
    investigating whether an offence has been committed under the
    [Criminal Code](/eng/acts/C-46), or the laying of an information or
    the preferring of an indictment, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} such information can reasonably be regarded as
      being relevant for the purpose of ascertaining the circumstances
      in which an offence under the [Criminal Code](/eng/acts/C-46) may
      have been committed, or the identity of the person or persons who
      may have committed an offence, with respect to an official, or
      with respect to any person related to that official,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the official was or is engaged in the
      administration or enforcement of this Part, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the offence can reasonably be considered to be
      related to that administration or enforcement;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} provide confidential information to any person
    solely for the purpose of enabling the Chief Statistician, within
    the meaning assigned by section 2 of the [Statistics
    Act](/eng/acts/S-19), to provide to a statistical agency of a
    province data concerning business activities carried on in the
    province, if the information is used by the statistical agency of
    the province solely for research and analysis and that statistical
    agency is authorized under the law of the province to collect the
    same or similar information on its own behalf in respect of such
    activities;

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} provide confidential information, or allow the
    inspection of or access to confidential information, as the case may
    be, solely for the purposes of a provision contained in a [[tax
    treaty]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} (as defined in subsection 248(1) of
    the [Income Tax Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3)) or in a listed international
    agreement; or

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} provide confidential information to a person who
    has --- under a program administered by the Canada Revenue Agency to
    obtain information relating to tax non-compliance --- entered into a
    contract to provide information to the Canada Revenue Agency, to the
    extent necessary to inform the person of any amount they may be
    entitled to under the contract and of the status of their claim
    under the contract.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restrictions on information sharing

  [(5.01)]{.lawlabel} No information may be provided to a representative
  of a government entity under paragraph (5)(j) in connection with a
  program, activity or service provided or undertaken by the government
  entity unless the government entity uses the business number as an
  identifier in connection with the program, activity or service.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Public disclosure

  [(5.02)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, in connection with a program,
  activity or service provided or undertaken by the Minister, make
  available to the public the business number of, and the name of
  (including any trade name or other name used by), the holder of a
  business number.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Public disclosure by representative of
  government entity

  [(5.03)]{.lawlabel} A representative of a government entity may, in
  connection with a program, activity or service provided or undertaken
  by the government entity, make available to the public the business
  number of, and the name of (including any trade name or other name
  used by), the holder of a business number, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a representative of the government entity was
    provided with that information pursuant to paragraph (5)(j); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the government entity uses the business number as
    an identifier in connection with the program, activity or service.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Serious offences

  [(5.04)]{.lawlabel} An official may provide to a law enforcement
  officer of an appropriate police organization

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} confidential information, if the official has
    reasonable grounds to believe that the information will afford
    evidence of an act or omission in or outside of Canada that, if
    committed in Canada, would be

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an offence under any of

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} section 3 of the [Corruption of Foreign Public
        Officials Act](/eng/acts/C-45.2),

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} sections 119 to 121, 123 to 125 and 426 of the
        [Criminal Code](/eng/acts/C-46),

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} section 465 of the [Criminal
        Code](/eng/acts/C-46) as it relates to an offence described in
        clause (B), and

      - [(D)]{.lawlabel} sections 144, 264, 271, 279, 279.02, 281 and
        333.1, paragraphs 334(a) and 348(1)(e) and sections 349, 435 and
        462.31 of the [Criminal Code](/eng/acts/C-46),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a terrorism offence or a criminal organization
      offence, as those terms are defined in section 2 of the [Criminal
      Code](/eng/acts/C-46), for which the maximum term of imprisonment
      is 10 years or more, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an offence

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} that is punishable by a minimum term of
        imprisonment,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} for which the maximum term of imprisonment is
        14 years or life, or

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} for which the maximum term of imprisonment is
        10 years and that

        - [(I)]{.lawlabel} resulted in bodily harm,

        - [(II)]{.lawlabel} involved the import, export, trafficking or
          production of drugs, or

        - [(III)]{.lawlabel} involved the use of a weapon; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} information setting out the reasonable grounds
    referred to in paragraph (a), to the extent that any such grounds
    rely on information referred to in that paragraph.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Threats to security

  [(5.05)]{.lawlabel} An official may provide to the head of a recipient
  Government of Canada institution listed in Schedule 3 to the Security
  of Canada Information Disclosure Act, or to an official designated for
  the purposes of that Act by the head of that recipient institution,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} confidential information, if there are reasonable
    grounds to suspect that the information would be relevant to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an investigation of whether the activity of any
      person may constitute threats to the security of Canada, as
      defined in section 2 of the [Canadian Security Intelligence
      Service Act](/eng/acts/C-23), or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an investigation of whether any of the following
      offences may have been committed:

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} a terrorism offence as defined in section 2 of
        the [Criminal Code](/eng/acts/C-46), and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} an offence under section 462.31 of the
        [Criminal Code](/eng/acts/C-46), if that investigation is
        related to a terrorism offence as defined in section 2 of that
        Act; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} information setting out the reasonable grounds
    referred to in paragraph (a), to the extent that any such grounds
    rely on information referred to in that paragraph.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Measures to prevent unauthorized use or
  disclosure

  [(5.1)]{.lawlabel} The person presiding at a legal proceeding relating
  to the supervision, evaluation or discipline of an authorized person
  may order such measures as are necessary to ensure that confidential
  information is not used or provided to any person for any purpose not
  relating to that proceeding, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} holding a hearing [in camera]{.otherLang
    lang="la"};

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} banning the publication of the information;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} concealing the identity of the person to whom the
    information relates; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} sealing the records of the proceeding.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disclosure to person or on consent

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} An official or other representative of a government
  entity may provide confidential information relating to a person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to that person; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with the consent of that person, to any other
    person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Confirmation of registration and
  business number

  [(6.1)]{.lawlabel} On being provided by any person with information
  specified by the Minister sufficient to identify a single person and a
  number, an official may confirm or deny that the following statements
  are both true:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the identified person is registered under
    Subdivision E of Division II or Subdivision D of Division V; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number is the business number of the identified
    person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Appeal from order or direction

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} An order or direction that is made in the course of
  or in connection with any legal proceedings and that requires an
  official or other representative of a government entity to give or
  produce evidence relating to any confidential information may, by
  notice served on all interested parties, be appealed forthwith by the
  Minister or by the person against whom the order or direction is made
  to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the court of appeal of the province in which the
    order or direction is made, in the case of an order or direction
    made by a court or other tribunal established under the laws of the
    province, whether that court or tribunal is exercising a
    jurisdiction conferred by the laws of Canada; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the Federal Court of Appeal, in the case of an
    order or direction made by a court or other tribunal established
    under the laws of Canada.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Disposition of appeal

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} The court to which an appeal is taken under
  subsection (7) may allow the appeal and quash the order or direction
  appealed from or may dismiss the appeal, and the rules of practice and
  procedure from time to time governing appeals to the courts shall
  apply, with such modifications as the circumstances require, in
  respect of an appeal instituted under subsection (7).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Stay

  [(9)]{.lawlabel} An appeal instituted under subsection (7) shall stay
  the operation of the order or direction appealed from until judgment
  is pronounced.

#### [SUBDIVISION D]{.HLabel3}[Assessments, Objections and Appeals]{.HTitleText3} {#h-198770 .Subheading}

##### [Assessments]{.HTitleText4} {#h-198771 .Subheading}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assessments

- **[[296]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-296 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Minister may assess

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the net tax of a person under Division V for a
    reporting period of the person,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any tax payable by a person under Division II, IV
    or IV.1,

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any penalty or interest payable by a person under
    this Part,

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any amount payable by a person under any of
    paragraphs 228(2.1)(b) and (2.3)(d), section 230.1 and paragraphs
    232.01(5)(c) and 232.02(4)(c), and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any amount which a person is liable to pay or remit
    under subsection 177(1.1) or Subdivision A or B.1 of Division VII,

  and may reassess or make an additional assessment of tax, net tax,
  penalty, interest or an amount referred to in paragraph (d) or (e).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Allowance of unclaimed credit

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where, in assessing the net tax of a person for a
  particular reporting period of the person, the Minister determines
  that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an amount (in this subsection referred to as the
    "allowable credit") would have been allowed as an input tax credit
    for the particular reporting period or as a deduction in determining
    the net tax for the particular reporting period if it had been
    claimed in a return under Division V for the particular reporting
    period filed on the day that is the day on or before which the
    return for the particular reporting period was required to be filed
    and the requirements, if any, of subsection 169(4) or 234(1)
    respecting documentation that apply in respect of the allowable
    credit had been met,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the allowable credit was not claimed by the person
    in a return filed before the day notice of the assessment is sent to
    the person or was so claimed but was disallowed by the Minister, and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the allowable credit would be allowed, as an input
    tax credit or deduction in determining the net tax for a reporting
    period of the person, if it were claimed in a return under Division
    V filed on the day notice of the assessment is sent to the person or
    would be disallowed if it were claimed in that return only because
    the period for claiming the allowable credit expired before that
    day,

  the Minister shall take the allowable credit into account in assessing
  the net tax for the particular reporting period as if the person had
  claimed the allowable credit in a return filed for the period.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Allowance of unclaimed rebate

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} Where, in assessing the net tax of a person for a
  reporting period of the person or an amount (in this subsection
  referred to as the "overdue amount") that became payable by a person
  under this Part, the Minister determines that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an amount (in this subsection referred to as the
    "allowable rebate") would have been payable to the person as a
    rebate if it had been claimed in an application under this Part
    filed on the particular day that is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the assessment is in respect of net tax for
      the reporting period, the day on or before which the return under
      Division V for the period was required to be filed, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the assessment is in respect of an overdue
      amount, the day on which the overdue amount became payable by the
      person,

    and, where the rebate is in respect of an amount that is being
    assessed, if the person had paid or remitted that amount,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the allowable rebate was not claimed by the person
    in an application filed before the day notice of the assessment is
    sent to the person, and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the allowable rebate would be payable to the person
    if it were claimed in an application under this Part filed on the
    day notice of the assessment is sent to the person or would be
    disallowed if it were claimed in that application only because the
    period for claiming the allowable rebate expired before that day,

  the Minister shall apply all or part of the allowable rebate against
  that net tax or overdue amount as if the person had, on the particular
  day, paid or remitted the amount so applied on account of that net tax
  or overdue amount

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application or payment of credit

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} If, in assessing the net tax of a person for a
  particular reporting period of the person, the Minister determines
  that there is an overpayment of net tax for the particular period,
  except where the assessment is made in the circumstances described in
  paragraph 298(4)(a) or (b) after the time otherwise limited for the
  assessment by paragraph 298(1)(a), the Minister shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} apply

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} all or part of the overpayment

    against

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any amount (in this paragraph referred to as the
      "outstanding amount") that, on or before the particular day that
      is the day on or before which the person was required to file a
      return under this Part for the particular period, the person
      defaulted in paying or remitting under this Part and that remains
      unpaid or unremitted on the day notice of the assessment is sent
      to the person,

    as if the person had, on the particular day, paid or remitted the
    amount so applied on account of the outstanding amount;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} apply

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} all or part of the overpayment that was not
      applied under paragraph (a) together with interest at the
      prescribed rate on all or that part of the overpayment, computed
      for the period beginning on the day that is 30 days after the
      latest of

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the particular day,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the day on which the return for the particular
        reporting period was filed, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an overpayment that is
        attributable to a payment or remittance made on a day subsequent
        to the days referred to in clauses (A) and (B), that subsequent
        day,

      and ending on the day on which the person defaulted in paying or
      remitting the outstanding amount referred to in subparagraph (ii)

    against

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any amount (in this paragraph referred to as the
      "outstanding amount") that, on a day (in this paragraph referred
      to as the "later day") after the particular day, the person
      defaulted in paying or remitting under this Part and that remains
      unpaid or unremitted on the day notice of the assessment is sent
      to the person,

    as if the person had, on the later day, paid the amount and interest
    so applied on account of the outstanding amount; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} refund to the person that part of the overpayment
    that was not applied under paragraphs (a) and (b) together with
    interest at the prescribed rate on that part of the overpayment,
    computed for the period beginning on the day that is 30 days after
    the latest of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the particular day,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the day on which the return for the particular
      reporting period was filed, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an overpayment that is
      attributable to a payment or remittance made on a day subsequent
      to the days referred to in subparagraphs (i) and (ii), that
      subsequent day,

    and ending on the day the refund is paid to the person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Application or payment of rebate

  [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} If, in assessing the net tax of a person for a
  particular reporting period of the person or an amount (in this
  subsection referred to as the "overdue amount") that became payable by
  a person under this Part, all or part of an allowable rebate referred
  to in subsection (2.1) is not applied under that subsection against
  that net tax or overdue amount, except where the assessment is made in
  the circumstances described in paragraph 298(4)(a) or (b) after the
  time otherwise limited for the assessment by paragraph 298(1)(a), the
  Minister shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} apply

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} all or part of the allowable rebate that was not
      applied under subsection (2.1)

    against

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any other amount (in this paragraph referred to
      as the "outstanding amount") that, on or before the particular day
      that is

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} if the assessment is in respect of net tax for
        the particular reporting period, the day on or before which the
        return under Division V for the particular period was required
        to be filed, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} if the assessment is in respect of an overdue
        amount, the day on which the overdue amount became payable by
        the person,

      the person defaulted in paying or remitting under this Part and
      that remains unpaid or unremitted on the day notice of the
      assessment is sent to the person,

    as if the person had, on the particular day, paid or remitted the
    amount so applied on account of the outstanding amount;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} apply

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} all or part of the allowable rebate that was not
      applied under subsection (2.1) or paragraph (a) together with
      interest at the prescribed rate on all or that part of the
      allowable rebate, computed for the period beginning on the day
      that is 30 days after the later of

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the particular day, and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} where the assessment is in respect of net tax
        for the particular reporting period, the day on which the return
        for the particular reporting period was filed,

      and ending on the day on which the person defaulted in paying or
      remitting the outstanding amount referred to in subparagraph (ii)

    against

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any amount (in this paragraph referred to as the
      "outstanding amount") that, on a day (in this paragraph referred
      to as the "later day") after the particular day, the person
      defaulted in paying or remitting under this Part and that remains
      unpaid or unremitted on the day notice of the assessment is sent
      to the person,

    as if the person had, on the later day, paid the amount and interest
    so applied on account of the outstanding amount; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} refund to the person that part of the allowable
    rebate that was not applied under any of subsection (2.1) and
    paragraphs (a) and (b) together with interest at the prescribed rate
    on that part of the allowable rebate, computed for the period
    beginning on the day that is 30 days after the later of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the particular day, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the assessment is in respect of net tax
      for the particular reporting period, the day on which the return
      for the particular period was filed,

    and ending on the day the refund is paid to the person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation on refunding overpayments

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An overpayment of net tax for a particular reporting
  period of a person and interest thereon under paragraphs (3)(b) and
  (c)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} shall not be applied under paragraph (3)(b) against
    an amount (in this paragraph referred to as the "outstanding
    amount") that is payable or remittable by the person unless the
    input tax credit or deduction to which the overpayment is
    attributable would have been allowed as an input tax credit or
    deduction, as the case may be, in determining the net tax for
    another reporting period of the person if the person had claimed the
    input tax credit or deduction in a return under Division V filed on
    the day the person defaulted in paying or remitting the outstanding
    amount and the person were not a specified person for the purposes
    of subsection 225(4); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} shall not be refunded under paragraph (3)(c) unless
    the input tax credit or deduction would have been allowed as an
    input tax credit or deduction, as the case may be, in determining
    the net tax for another reporting period of the person if the person
    had claimed the input tax credit or deduction in a return under
    Division V filed on the day notice of the assessment is sent to the
    person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation on refunding allowable
  rebates

  [(4.1)]{.lawlabel} An allowable rebate referred to in subsection (2.1)
  or a part thereof that was not applied under that subsection and
  interest thereon under paragraphs (3.1)(b) and (c)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} shall not be applied under paragraph (3.1)(b)
    against an amount (in this paragraph referred to as the "outstanding
    amount") that is payable or remittable by a person unless the
    allowable rebate would have been payable to the person as a rebate
    if the person had claimed it in an application under this Part filed
    on the day the person defaulted in paying or remitting the
    outstanding amount and, in the case of a rebate under section 261,
    if subsection 261(3) allowed the person to claim the rebate within
    four years after the person paid or remitted the amount in respect
    of which the rebate would be so payable; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} shall not be refunded under paragraph (3.1)(c)
    unless the allowable rebate would have been payable to the person as
    a rebate if the person had claimed it in an application under this
    Part filed on the day notice of the assessment is sent to the
    person, and, where the rebate is in respect of an amount that is
    being assessed, if the person had paid or remitted that amount.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Deemed claim or application

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where, in assessing the net tax of a person or tax or
  any other amount payable by a person, the Minister takes an amount
  into account under subsection (2) or applies or refunds an amount
  under subsection (2.1), (3) or (3.1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person is deemed to have claimed the amount in
    a return or application filed under this Part; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} to the extent that an amount is applied against any
    tax or other amount payable or remittable by the person under this
    Part, the Minister is deemed to have refunded or paid the amount to
    the person and the person is deemed to have paid or remitted the tax
    or other amount against which it was applied.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Refund on reassessment

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Where a person has paid an amount on account of tax,
  net tax, penalty, interest or other amount assessed under this section
  and the amount paid exceeds the amount determined on reassessment to
  have been payable or remittable by the person, the Minister shall
  refund to the person the amount of the excess, together with interest
  thereon at the prescribed rate for the period beginning on the day the
  amount was paid by the person and ending on the day the refund is
  paid.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Interest on cancelled amounts

  [(6.1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (6), if a person has paid an
  amount of interest or penalty and the Minister cancels that amount
  under section 281.1, the Minister shall refund the amount to the
  person, together with interest on the amount at the prescribed rate
  for the period beginning on the day that is 30 days after the day on
  which the Minister received a request in a manner satisfactory to the
  Minister to apply that section and ending on the day on which the
  refund is paid.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Restriction on refunds

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} An amount under this section shall not be refunded to
  a person at any time unless all returns of which the Minister has
  knowledge and that are required to be filed at or before that time by
  the person under this Act, the [Income Tax Act](/eng/acts/I-3.3), the
  [Air Travellers Security Charge Act](/eng/acts/A-10.5), the [Excise
  Act, 2001](/eng/acts/E-14.1), the [Underused Housing Tax
  Act](/eng/acts/U-0.5), the [Select Luxury Items Tax
  Act](/eng/acts/S-8.35), the [Digital Services Tax
  Act](/eng/acts/D-1.65) and the [Global Minimum Tax
  Act](/eng/acts/G-3.3) have been filed with the Minister.

- Meaning of [[overpayment of net tax]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} In this section, [[overpayment of net
  tax]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} of a person for a reporting period of the
  person means the amount, if any, by which the total of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all amounts remitted by the person on account of
    net tax for the period, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the net tax for the period is negative, the
    net tax refund for the period,

  exceeds the total of

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} where the net tax for the period is positive, the
    net tax for the period, and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} all amounts paid to the person as a net tax refund
    for the period.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assessment of rebate

- **[[297]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-297 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} On
  receipt of an application made by a person for a rebate under section
  215.1 or Division VI, the Minister shall, with all due dispatch,
  consider the application and assess the amount of the rebate, if any,
  payable to the person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Reassessment

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may reassess or make an additional
  assessment of the amount of a rebate, notwithstanding any previous
  assessment of the amount of the rebate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assessment of overpayment of rebate

  [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may assess, reassess or make an
  additional assessment of an amount payable by a person under section
  264, notwithstanding any previous assessment of the amount.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Payment of rebate

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where, on assessment under this section, the Minister
  determines that a rebate is payable to a person, the Minister shall
  pay the rebate to the person.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Interest on rebate

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a rebate under section 215.1 or Division VI (other
  than section 253) is paid to a person under subsection (3), the
  Minister shall pay interest at the prescribed rate to the person on
  the rebate for the period beginning on the day that is 30 days after
  the day the application in which the rebate is claimed is filed with
  the Minister and ending on the day the rebate is paid.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, 2006, c. 4, s. 152\]]{.Repealed}

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minimum amounts owed to Her Majesty

- **[[297.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-297.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister determines, at any
  time, that the total of all amounts owing by a person to Her Majesty
  in right of Canada under this Part does not exceed two dollars, those
  amounts are deemed to be nil.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minimum amounts payable by Minister

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, at any time, the total of all amounts payable by
  the Minister to a person under this Part does not exceed two dollars,
  the Minister may apply those amounts against any amount owing, at that
  time, by the person to Her Majesty in right of Canada. However, if the
  person, at that time, does not owe any amount to Her Majesty in right
  of Canada, those amounts payable are deemed to be nil.

::: HistoricalNote
- \[NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated
  text
- see relevant amending Acts and regulations.\]
- 2006, c. 4, s. 153
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Period for assessment

- **[[298]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-298
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) to (6.1),
  an assessment of a person shall not be made under section 296

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an assessment of net tax of the person for a
      reporting period of the person,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an amount payable under section 230.1 in respect
      of an amount paid to, or applied to a liability of, the person as
      a refund under Division V in respect of a reporting period of the
      person, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an amount payable under section 230.1 in
      respect of an amount paid to, or applied to a liability of, the
      person as interest under Division V in respect of an amount paid
      or applied as a refund in respect of a reporting period of the
      person,

    more than four years after the later of the day on or before which
    the person was required under section 238 to file a return for the
    period and the day the return was filed;

  - [(a.01)]{.lawlabel} despite paragraph (a), in the case of an
    assessment of the net tax of the person for a reporting period of
    the person that is made solely to take into account an amount of tax
    payable under section 218.01, more than seven years after the later
    of the day on or before which the person was required under section
    238 to file a return for the period and the day the return was
    filed;

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an assessment of an amount payable
    under paragraph 228(2.1)(b) or (2.3)(d), 232.01(5)(c) or
    232.02(4)(c) that a person is required to pay on or before a day,
    more than four years after that day;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an assessment of tax payable by the
    person under Division II in respect of a supply to which subsection
    221(2) or (2.1) applies, more than four years after the later of the
    day on or before which the person was required to file the return in
    which that tax was required to be reported and the day the return
    was filed;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an assessment of tax payable by the
    person under Division II, other than tax referred to in paragraph
    (b), more than four years after the tax became payable;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an assessment of tax payable by the
    person under Division IV,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the tax is payable under section 218.01 or
      subsection 218.1(1.2), more than seven years after the later of
      the day on or before which the person was required to file the
      return in which that tax was required to be reported and the day
      the return was filed, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, more than four years after
      the later of the day on or before which the person was required to
      file the return in which that tax was required to be reported and
      the day the return was filed;

  - [(d.1)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an assessment of tax payable by
    the person under Division IV.1, more than four years after

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} where the person is required to report the tax in
      a return, the later of the day on or before which the person was
      required to file the return with the Minister and the day the
      return was filed, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, the day the person is
      required to pay the tax to the Receiver General;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in the case of any penalty payable by the person,
    other than a penalty under section 280.1, 285, 285.01, 285.02,
    285.03 or 285.1, more than four years after the person became liable
    to pay the penalty;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an assessment of an amount for which
    a person became liable under subsection 177(1.1), section 266 or
    267.1, subsection 270(4) or Subdivision B.1 of Division VII, more
    than four years after the person became liable; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an assessment for an amount for
    which a trustee in bankruptcy became liable under Subdivision A of
    Division VII, after the earlier of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the day that is ninety days after the return
      under this Part on which the assessment is based is filed with, or
      other evidence of the facts on which the assessment is based comes
      to the attention of, the Minister, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the expiration of the period determined under
      whichever of paragraphs (a) to (e) applies in the circumstances.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Period for assessment of rebate

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) to (6.1), an assessment
  under subsection 297(1) of the amount of a rebate may be made at any
  time, but a reassessment or additional assessment under section 297 or
  an assessment under subsection 297(2.1) in respect of an amount paid
  or applied as a rebate or of an amount paid or applied as interest in
  respect of an amount paid or applied as a rebate shall not be made
  more than four years after the day the application for the rebate was
  filed in accordance with this Part.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (1) and (2) do not apply in respect of a
  reassessment of a person made

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to give effect to a decision on an objection or
    appeal;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with the consent in writing of the person to
    dispose of an appeal; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} to give effect to an alternative basis or argument
    advanced by the Minister under subsection (6.1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An assessment in respect of any matter may be made at
  any time where the person to be assessed has, in respect of that
  matter,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} made a misrepresentation that is attributable to
    the person's neglect, carelessness or wilful default;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} committed fraud

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in making or filing a return under this Part,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in making or filing an application for a rebate
      under Division VI, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in supplying, or failing to supply, any
      information under this Part; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} filed a waiver under subsection (7) that is in
    effect at that time.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where, in making an assessment, the Minister
  determines that a person has paid in respect of any matter an amount
  as or an account of tax payable or net tax remittable for a particular
  reporting period of the person that was in fact payable or remittable
  for another reporting period of the person, the Minister may at any
  time make an assessment for that other period in respect of that
  matter.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Idem

  [(6)]{.lawlabel} Where the result of a reassessment on an objection
  to, or a decision on an appeal from, an assessment is to reduce the
  amount of tax payable by a person and, by reason of the reduction, any
  input tax credit or rebate claimed by the person for a reporting
  period, or in an application for a rebate, should be reduced, the
  Minister may assess or reassess that reporting period or that
  application for rebate, as the case may be, only for the purpose of
  taking the reduction of tax into account in respect of the input tax
  credit or rebate.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Alternative basis or argument

  [(6.1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may advance an alternative basis or
  argument in support of an assessment of a person, or in support of all
  or any portion of the total amount determined on assessment to be
  payable or remittable by a person under this Part, at any time after
  the period otherwise limited by subsection (1) or (2) for making the
  assessment unless, on an appeal under this Part,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} there is relevant evidence that the person is no
    longer able to adduce without leave of the court; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is not appropriate in the circumstances for the
    court to order that the evidence be adduced.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Limitation

  [(6.2)]{.lawlabel} If a reassessment of a person is made that gives
  effect to an alternative basis or argument advanced by the Minister
  under subsection (6.1) in support of a particular assessment of the
  person, the Minister shall not reassess for an amount that is greater
  than the total amount of the particular assessment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Exception

  [(6.3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (6.2) does not apply to any portion of
  an amount determined on reassessment that the Minister would be
  entitled to reassess under this Part at any time after the period
  otherwise limited by subsection (1) or (2) for making the reassessment
  if this Part were read without reference to subsection (6.1).

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Waiver

  [(7)]{.lawlabel} Any person may, within the time otherwise limited by
  subsection (1) or (2) for assessing the person, waive the application
  of subsection (1) or (2) by filing with the Minister a waiver in the
  prescribed form specifying the matter in respect of which the person
  waives the application of that subsection.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Revoking waiver

  [(8)]{.lawlabel} Any person who files a waiver under subsection (7)
  may revoke the waiver on six months notice to the Minister by filing
  with the Minister a notice of revocation of the waiver in the
  prescribed form.

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Minister not bound

- **[[299]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-299 .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The
  Minister is not bound by any return, application or information
  provided by or on behalf of any person and may make an assessment,
  notwithstanding any return, application or information so provided or
  that no return, application or information has been provided.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Liability not affected

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} Liability under this Part to pay or remit any tax,
  penalty, interest or other amount is not affected by an incorrect or
  incomplete assessment or by the fact that no assessment has been made.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assessment valid and binding

  [(3)]{.lawlabel} An assessment, subject to being vacated on an
  objection or appeal under this Part and subject to a reassessment,
  shall be deemed to be valid and binding.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Binding effect where unincorporated
  body

  [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} Where a person (referred to in this subsection as
  the "body") that is not an individual or a corporation is assessed in
  respect of any matter,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the assessment is not invalid only because one or
    more other persons (each of which is referred to in this subsection
    as a "representative") who are liable for obligations of the body
    did not receive a notice of the assessment;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the assessment is binding on each representative of
    the body, subject to a reassessment of the body and the rights of
    the body to object to or appeal from the assessment under this Part;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an assessment of a representative in respect of the
    same matter is binding on the representative subject only to a
    reassessment of the representative and the rights of the
    representative to object to or appeal from the assessment of the
    representative under this Part on the grounds that the
    representative is not a person who is liable to pay or remit an
    amount to which the assessment of the body relates, the body has
    been reassessed in respect of that matter or the assessment of the
    body in respect of that matter has been vacated.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Assessment deemed valid

  [(4)]{.lawlabel} An assessment shall, subject to being reassessed or
  vacated as a result of an objection or appeal under this Part, be
  deemed to be valid and binding, notwithstanding any error, defect or
  omission therein or in any proceeding under this Part relating
  thereto.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Irregularities

  [(5)]{.lawlabel} An appeal from an assessment shall not be allowed by
  reasons only of an irregularity, informality, omission or error on the
  part of any person in the observation of any directory provision of
  this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- \[NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Notice of assessment

- **[[300]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-300
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} After making an assessment, the
  Minister shall send to the person assessed a notice of the assessment.

- [Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Scope of notice

  [(2)]{.lawlabel} A notice of assessment may include assessments in
  respect of any number or combination of reporting periods,
  transactions, rebates or amounts payable or remittable under this
  Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- \[NOTE: Application provisions are not included in the consolidated
  text
- see relevant amending Acts and regulations.\]
- 1990, c. 45, s. 12
- 1997, c. 10, s. 81
:::

[Marginal note:]{.wb-invisible}Amount deemed not assessed

**[[300.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-300.1 .sectionLabel}** Despite any other
provision of this Part, an amount in respect of which particular
information relevant to its assessment was provided to the Canada
Revenue Agency under a contract entered into by a person under a program
administered by the Canada Revenue Agency to obtain information relating
to tax non-compliance is, until the amount is collected by the Minister,
deemed for the purpose of any agreement entered into by or on behalf of
the Government of Canada under section 8.3 of the [Federal-Provincial
Fiscal Arrangements Act](/eng/acts/F-7.8) not to be payable or
remittable under this Part as a result of an assessment.
