## [SCHEDULE IX]{.scheduleLabel}[(Section 144.1)]{.OriginatingRef}[Supply in a Province]{.scheduleTitleText}  {#h-201850 .scheduleLabel}
:::

## PART I Interpretation {#part-i-interpretation .SchedHeadL1}

- [1]{.lawlabel} The definitions in this section apply in this Schedule.

  [[lease interval]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in respect of a supply by way
  of lease, licence or similar arrangement, has the same meaning as in
  section 136.1 of the Act.

  [[place of negotiation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} of a supply means the
  location of the supplier's permanent establishment at which the
  individual principally involved in negotiating for the supplier the
  agreement for the supply ordinarily works, or to which that individual
  ordinarily reports, in the performance of the individual's duties in
  relation to the activities of the supplier in the course of which the
  supply is made and, for the purposes of this definition,
  [[negotiating]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes the making or acceptance
  of an offer.

- [2]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Schedule,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a floating home, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a mobile home that is not affixed to land

  are each deemed to be tangible personal property and not real
  property.

- [3]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Schedule, where an agreement
  for the supply of property or a service is entered into but the
  property is never delivered to the recipient or the service is never
  performed, the property is deemed to have been delivered, or the
  service is deemed to have been performed, where the property or
  service was to be delivered or performed, as the case may be, under
  the terms of the agreement.

- [4]{.lawlabel} Where, for the purpose of determining, under this
  Schedule, if a supply is made in a province, reference is made to the
  ordinary location of property and, from time to time, the supplier and
  recipient mutually agree upon what is to be the ordinary location of
  the property at a particular time, that location is deemed, for the
  purposes of this Schedule, to be the ordinary location of that
  property at the particular time.

- [5]{.lawlabel} The definition [[courier]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in
  subsection 123(1) does not apply for the purposes of this Schedule.

## PART II Tangible Personal Property {#part-ii-tangible-personal-property .SchedHeadL1}

- [1]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 3 of Part VI, a supply by way of
  sale of tangible personal property is made in a province if the
  supplier delivers the property or makes it available in the province
  to the recipient of the supply.

- [2]{.lawlabel} A supply of tangible personal property otherwise than
  by way of sale is made in a province if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a supply made under an agreement
    under which continuous possession or use of the property is provided
    for a period of no more than three months, the supplier delivers the
    property or makes it available in the province to the recipient of
    the supply; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} where the property is a specified motor vehicle,
      it is required, at the time the supply is made, to be registered
      under the laws of the province relating to the registration of
      motor vehicles, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the property is not a specified motor
      vehicle, the ordinary location of the property, as determined at
      the time the supply is made, is in the province.

- [3]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part and Part VII, property is
  deemed to be delivered in a particular province by a supplier and is
  deemed not to be delivered in any other province by the supplier where
  the supplier

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} ships the property to a destination in the
    particular province that is specified in the contract for carriage
    of the property or transfers possession of the property to a common
    carrier or consignee that the supplier has retained on behalf of the
    recipient to ship the property to such a destination; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} sends the property by mail or courier to an address
    in the particular province.

- [4]{.lawlabel} If

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a supply of tangible personal property is made by
    way of lease, licence or similar arrangement under which continuous
    possession or use of the property is provided for a period of no
    more than three months,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} because of paragraph 136.1(1)(a) of the Act, there
    is deemed to be more than one supply of the property under that
    arrangement, and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the absence of that paragraph, the supply of the
    property under that arrangement would be made in a province,

  all the supplies of the property that are, because of that paragraph,
  deemed to be made under that arrangement are made in that province.

## PART III Intangible Personal Property {#part-iii-intangible-personal-property .SchedHeadL1}

- [1]{.lawlabel} In this Part, [[Canadian rights]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm},
  in respect of intangible personal property, means that part of the
  property that can be used in Canada.

- [2]{.lawlabel} A supply of intangible personal property is made in a
  province if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of property that relates to real
    property,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} all or substantially all of the real property
      that is situated in Canada is situated in the province, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the place of negotiation of the supply is in the
      province and it is not the case that all or substantially all of
      the real property is situated outside the province;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of property that relates to tangible
    personal property,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} all or substantially all of the tangible personal
      property that is ordinarily located in Canada is ordinarily
      located in the province, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the place of negotiation of the supply is in the
      province and it is not the case that all or substantially all of
      the tangible personal property is ordinarily located outside the
      province;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of property that relates to services to
    be performed,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} all or substantially all of the services that are
      to be performed in Canada are to be performed in the province, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the place of negotiation of the supply is in the
      province and it is not the case that all or substantially all of
      the services are to be performed outside the province; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in any other case,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} all or substantially all of the Canadian rights
      in respect of the property can be used only in the province, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the place of negotiation of the supply is in the
      province and the property can be used otherwise than exclusively
      outside the province.

- [3]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 2, where a supply of intangible
  personal property is made and

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of intangible personal property that
    relates to real property,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the real property that is situated in Canada is
      situated primarily in the participating provinces, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the place of negotiation of the supply is
      outside Canada, all or substantially all of the real property is
      situated in Canada,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of intangible personal property that
    relates to tangible personal property,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the tangible personal property that is ordinarily
      located in Canada is ordinarily located primarily in the
      participating provinces, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the place of negotiation of the supply is
      outside Canada, all or substantially all of the personal property
      is ordinarily located in Canada,

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of intangible personal property that
    relates to services to be performed,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the services to be performed in Canada are to be
      performed primarily in the participating provinces, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the place of negotiation of the supply is
      outside Canada, all or substantially all of the services are to be
      performed in Canada, and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of intangible personal property that
    does not relate to real property, tangible personal property or
    services to be performed,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the Canadian rights in respect of the intangible
      personal property cannot be used otherwise than primarily in the
      participating provinces, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the place of negotiation of the supply is
      outside Canada, the property cannot be used otherwise than
      exclusively in Canada,

  the supply of the intangible personal property is made in the
  participating province in which the greatest proportion of the real
  property that is situated in the participating provinces is situated,
  the tangible personal property ordinarily located in the participating
  provinces is ordinarily located, the services to be performed in the
  participating provinces are to be performed, or the Canadian rights
  that can be used only in the participating provinces can be used, as
  the case may be.

## PART IV Real Property {#part-iv-real-property .SchedHeadL1}

- [1]{.lawlabel} A supply of real property is made in a province if the
  property is situated in the province.

- [2]{.lawlabel} A supply of a service in relation to real property is
  made in a province if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all or substantially all of the real property that
    is situated in Canada is situated in the province; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the place of negotiation of the supply is in the
    province and it is not the case that all or substantially all of the
    real property is situated outside the province.

- [3]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 2, where a supply of a service in
  relation to real property is made and the real property that is
  situated in Canada is situated primarily in participating provinces,
  the supply is made in the participating province in which the greatest
  proportion of the real property that is situated in the participating
  provinces is situated, unless the place of negotiation of the supply
  is outside Canada and it is not the case that all or substantially all
  of the property is situated in Canada.

## PART V Services {#part-v-services .SchedHeadL1}

- [1]{.lawlabel} In this Part, [[Canadian element]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
  of a service means the portion of the service that is performed in
  Canada.

- [2]{.lawlabel} Subject to Parts IV and VI to VIII, a supply of a
  service is made in a province if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all or substantially all of the Canadian element of
    the service is performed in the province; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the place of negotiation of the supply is in the
    province and it is not the case that all or substantially all of the
    service is performed outside the province.

- [3]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 2, where the Canadian element of a
  service is performed primarily in the participating provinces, the
  supply of the service is made in the participating province in which
  the greatest proportion of the Canadian element is performed, unless
  the place of negotiation of the supply is outside Canada and it is not
  the case that all or substantially all of the service is performed in
  Canada.

## PART VI Transportation Services {#part-vi-transportation-services .SchedHeadL1}

- [1]{.lawlabel} The definitions in this section apply in this Part.

  [[continuous journey]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the meaning assigned by
  section 1 of Part VII of Schedule VI.

  [[destination]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} of a freight transportation
  service means the place specified by the shipper of the property where
  possession of the property is transferred to the person to whom the
  property is consigned or addressed by the shipper.

  [[freight transportation service]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the meaning
  assigned by section 1 of Part VII of Schedule VI.

  [[leg]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} of a journey on a conveyance means a part
  of the journey that begins where passengers embark or disembark the
  conveyance or where it is stopped to allow for its servicing or
  refuelling and ends where it is next stopped for any of those
  purposes.

  [[origin]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} of a continuous journey has the meaning
  assigned by section 1 of Part VII of Schedule VI.

  [[stopover]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in respect of a continuous journey,
  has the meaning assigned by section 1 of Part VII of Schedule VI
  except that it does not include, in the case of a continuous journey
  of an individual or group of individuals that does not include
  transportation by air and the origin and termination of which are in
  Canada, any place outside Canada where, at the time the journey
  begins, the individual or group is not scheduled to be outside Canada
  for an uninterrupted period of at least 24 hours during the course of
  the journey.

  [[termination]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} of a continuous journey has the
  meaning assigned by section 1 of Part VII of Schedule VI.

- [2]{.lawlabel} A supply of a passenger transportation service that is
  part of a continuous journey is made in a province if,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the ticket or voucher issued in respect of
    the passenger transportation service included in the continuous
    journey that is provided first specifies the origin of the
    continuous journey, the origin is a place in the province and the
    termination, and all stopovers, in respect of the continuous journey
    are in Canada; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, the place of negotiation of the
    supply is in the province.

- [3]{.lawlabel} Where a supply by way of sale of tangible personal
  property or a service (other than a passenger transportation service)
  is made to an individual on board a conveyance in the course of a
  business of supplying passenger transportation services and physical
  possession of the property is transferred to the individual, or the
  service is wholly performed, on board the conveyance during any leg of
  the journey that begins in any participating province and ends in any
  participating province, the supply is made in the participating
  province in which that leg of the journey begins.

- [4]{.lawlabel} A supply of any of the following services made by a
  person in connection with the supply by that person of a passenger
  transportation service is made in a province if the supply of the
  passenger transportation service is made in the province:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a service of transporting an individual's baggage;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a service of supervising an unaccompanied child.

- [4.1]{.lawlabel} A supply by a person of a service of issuing,
  delivering, amending, replacing or cancelling a ticket, voucher or
  reservation for a supply by that person of a passenger transportation
  service is made in a province if the supply of the passenger
  transportation service would, if it were completed in accordance with
  the agreement for that supply, be made in the province.

- [5]{.lawlabel} Subject to Part VII, a supply of a freight
  transportation service is made in a province if the destination of the
  service is in the province.

## PART VII Postage {#part-vii-postage .SchedHeadL1}

- [1]{.lawlabel} The definitions in this section apply in this Part.

  [[postage stamp]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[timbre-poste]{.DefinedTermLink
  lang="fr"}

  [[postage stamp]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a stamp authorized by the
  Canada Post Corporation for use as evidence of the payment of postage,
  but does not include a postage meter impression, a permit imprint or
  any "business reply" indicia or item bearing that indicia.

  [[permit imprint]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[marque de
  permis]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"}

  [[permit imprint]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an indicia the use of
  which as evidence of the payment of postage exclusively by a person is
  authorized under an agreement between the Canada Post Corporation and
  the person, but does not include a postage meter impression or any
  "business reply" indicia or item bearing that indicia.

- [2]{.lawlabel} A supply of a postage stamp or a postage-paid card,
  package or similar item (other than an item bearing a "business reply"
  indicia) that is authorized by the Canada Post Corporation is made in
  a province if the supplier delivers the stamp or item in the province
  to the recipient of the supply and, where the stamp or item is used as
  evidence of the payment of postage for a mail delivery service, the
  supply of the service is made in that province, unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the supply of the service is made pursuant to a
    bill of lading; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the consideration for the supply of the service is
    \$5 or more and the address to which the mail is sent is not in a
    participating province.

- [3]{.lawlabel} Where the payment of postage for a mail delivery
  service supplied by the Canada Post Corporation is evidenced by a
  postage meter impression printed by a meter, the supply of the service
  is made in a province if the ordinary location of the meter, as
  determined at the time the recipient of the supply pays an amount to
  the Corporation for the purpose of paying that postage, is in the
  province, unless the supply is made pursuant to a bill of lading.

- [4]{.lawlabel} Where the payment of postage for a mail delivery
  service supplied by the Canada Post Corporation otherwise than
  pursuant to a bill of lading is evidenced by a permit imprint, the
  supply of the service is made in the province in which the recipient
  of the supply deposits the mail with the Corporation in accordance
  with the agreement between the recipient and the Corporation
  authorizing the use of the permit imprint.

## PART VIII Telecommunication Services {#part-viii-telecommunication-services .SchedHeadL1}

- [1]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, the billing location for
  a telecommunication service supplied to a recipient is in a province
  if,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the consideration paid or payable for the
    service is charged or applied to an account that the recipient has
    with a person who carries on the business of supplying
    telecommunication services and the account relates to
    telecommunications facilities that are used or are available for use
    by the recipient to obtain telecommunication services, all those
    telecommunications facilities are ordinarily located in the
    province; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, the telecommunications facility
    used to initiate the service is located in the province.

- [2]{.lawlabel} A supply of a telecommunication service (other than a
  service referred to in section 3) is made in a province if,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a telecommunication service of
    making telecommunications facilities available,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} all of those facilities are ordinarily located in
      the province, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where not all of those telecommunications
      facilities are ordinarily located in the province, the invoice for
      the supply of the service is sent to an address in the province;
      and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the telecommunication is emitted and received in
      the province,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the telecommunication is emitted or received in
      the province and the billing location for the service is in the
      province, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the telecommunication is emitted in the
      province and is received outside the province and the billing
      location for the service is not in a province in which the
      telecommunication is emitted or received.

- [3]{.lawlabel} A supply of a telecommunication service of granting to
  the recipient of the supply sole access to a telecommunications
  channel, within the meaning assigned by section 136.4 of the Act, is
  made in a province if the supply is deemed under that section to be
  made in the province.

## PART IX Deemed Supplies and Prescribed Supplies {#part-ix-deemed-supplies-and-prescribed-supplies .SchedHeadL1}

- [1]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding any other Part of this Schedule, a
  supply of property that is deemed under any of sections 129, 129.1,
  171, 171.1 and 172, subsections 183(1) and (4) and 184(1) and (3) and
  sections 196.1 and 268 of the Act to have been made or received at any
  time is made where the property is situated at that time.

- [2]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding any other Part of this Schedule, a
  supply of property or a service is made in a province if the supply is
  deemed under Part IX of the Act or regulations made under that Part to
  be made in the province.

- [3]{.lawlabel} Notwithstanding any other Part of this Schedule, a
  supply of property or a service is made in a province if the supply is
  prescribed to be made in the province.

- 2000, c. 30, ss. 136(F), 137, 138

## [SCHEDULE X]{.scheduleLabel}[Non-Taxable Property and Services for Purposes of Division IV.1 of Part IX]{.scheduleTitleText}  {#h-201977 .scheduleLabel}
:::

## PART I Non-Taxable Property for Purposes of Subdivision A {#part-i-non-taxable-property-for-purposes-of-subdivision-a .SchedHeadL1}

(*Subsections 220.05(3) and 220.06(3)*)

- [1]{.lawlabel} Property that is at any time brought into a
  participating province and that is described in heading No. 98.01,
  98.10 or 98.12 of Schedule I to the [Customs
  Tariff](/eng/acts/C-54.011) to the extent that the property would not
  be subject to customs duties under that Act.

- [2]{.lawlabel} Conveyances temporarily brought into a participating
  province, by a person who is resident in that province, to be employed
  in the international non-commercial transportation of that person and
  accompanying persons using the same conveyance.

- [3]{.lawlabel} Conveyances and baggage temporarily brought into a
  participating province by a non-resident person for use by that person
  in that province.

- [4]{.lawlabel} Arms, military stores and munitions of war brought into
  a participating province by the Government of Canada in replacement of
  or in anticipation or actual exchange for similar goods loaned to or
  exchanged or to be exchanged with the governments of a foreign country
  designated by the Governor in Council under heading No. 98.10 of
  Schedule I to the [Customs Tariff](/eng/acts/C-54.011), under such
  regulations as the Minister of Public Safety and Emergency
  Preparedness may make for purposes of heading No. 98.11 of that Act.

- [5]{.lawlabel} Property that is clothing or books brought into a
  participating province for charitable purposes, and photographs, not
  exceeding three, where they are brought into a participating province
  other than for the purpose of sale.

- [6]{.lawlabel} Property (other than advertising matter or excisable
  goods) that is a casual donation sent by a person in a
  non-participating province to a person in a participating province, or
  brought into a particular participating province by a person who is
  not resident in the participating provinces as a gift to a person in
  that participating province, where the fair market value of the
  property does not exceed \$60, under such regulations as the Minister
  of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness may make for purposes of
  heading No. 98.16 of Schedule I to the [Customs
  Tariff](/eng/acts/C-54.011).

- [7]{.lawlabel} Property that is brought into a participating province
  for a period not exceeding six months for the purpose of display at a
  convention (within the meaning assigned by the Display Goods Temporary
  Importation Regulations made under the [Customs
  Tariff](/eng/acts/C-54.011)) or a public exhibition at which the goods
  of various manufacturers or producers are displayed.

- [8]{.lawlabel} Property that is brought into a participating province
  on a temporary basis after having been removed from Mexico or the
  United States, where the property is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} intended for display or demonstration;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} commercial samples;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} advertising films; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} conveyances or containers based in the United
    States or Mexico engaged in the international traffic of goods.

- [9]{.lawlabel} Property that is at any time brought into a
  participating province by an individual who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} was formerly resident in the participating province
    and is, at that time, returning to resume residence in the
    participating province after being resident in another province for
    a period of not less than one year,

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is a resident of the participating province who is,
    at that time, returning after being absent from the participating
    province for a period of not less than one year, or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is, at that time, entering the province with the
    intention of establishing a residence for a period of not less than
    twelve months, (other than a person who enters Canada in order to
    reside in Canada for the purpose of employment for a temporary
    period not exceeding 36 months or for the purpose of studying at an
    institute of learning)

  where the property is for the individual's personal or household use
  and was owned and in the individual's possession before that time,
  provided that, where the property was owned and in the individual's
  possession for less than 31 days prior to the time when it is brought
  into the participating province

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the individual has paid any retail sales tax
    applicable to the property in the province from which the property
    has been brought, and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the individual is not entitled to claim a rebate or
    a refund of that retail sales tax.

- [10]{.lawlabel} Property that is brought into a participating
  province, where the property is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} personal and household effects of an individual who
    died outside the participating provinces and was, at the time of
    death, resident in a participating province, or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} personal and household effects received, by an
    individual who is resident in a participating province, as a result
    or in anticipation of the death of an individual who was not
    resident in a participating province,

  where the property is given as a gift or bequest to an individual who
  is resident in a participating province.

- [11]{.lawlabel} Medals, trophies and other prizes, not including usual
  merchantable goods, that are won outside the participating provinces
  in competitions, that are bestowed, received or accepted outside the
  participating provinces or that are donated by persons outside the
  participating provinces, for heroic deeds, valour or distinction.

- [12]{.lawlabel} Printed matter that is to be made available to the
  general public, without charge, for the promotion of tourism, where
  the printed matter is brought into a participating province

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by or on the order of a foreign government or a
    government outside the participating province or by an agency or
    representative of such a government; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} by a board of trade, chamber of commerce, municipal
    or automobile association or similar organization to which it was
    supplied for no consideration, other than shipping and handling
    charges.

- [13]{.lawlabel} Property that is brought into a participating province
  by a charity or a public institution and that has been donated to the
  charity or the institution.

- [14]{.lawlabel} Property that is brought into a participating province
  by a person if it is supplied to the person for no consideration,
  other than shipping and handling charges, as a replacement part or as
  replacement property under a warranty.

- [15]{.lawlabel} Property that is brought into a participating
  province, the supply of which is included in any of Parts I to IV and
  VIII of Schedule VI.

- [15.1]{.lawlabel} Property that is brought into a participating
  province during the eligible period, as defined in section 1 of Part
  XI of Schedule VI, and the supply of which would be included in that
  Part if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} sections 3 to 10 and 12 of that Part were each read
    without reference to "that is an eligible supply"; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the reference to "a supply that is an eligible
    supply and that would be a supply" in section 11 of that Part were
    read as a reference to "a supply that would be".

- [16]{.lawlabel} Containers that are brought into a participating
  province where, because of regulations made under Note 11(c) to
  Chapter 98 of Schedule I to the [Customs Tariff](/eng/acts/C-54.011),
  they would, if they were imported, be imported free of customs duties
  under that Act.

- [17]{.lawlabel} Money or certificates or other documents evidencing a
  right that is a financial instrument.

- [18]{.lawlabel} Property that is brought into a participating province
  by a person after having been supplied to the person by another person
  in circumstances in which tax was payable in respect of the property
  by the person under subsection 165(2) or section 218.1 of the Act.

- [19]{.lawlabel} Property that a person brings at any time into a
  participating province and that at that time is being supplied in a
  non-participating province to the person by way of lease, licence or
  similar arrangement under which continuous possession or use of the
  property is provided for a period of more than three months and in
  circumstances in which tax under subsection 165(1) is payable by the
  person in respect of that supply.

- [20]{.lawlabel} Property that is brought into a participating province
  by a person after having been imported by the person in circumstances
  in which

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} tax was not payable under section 212 of the Act in
    respect of the property because of section 213 of the Act; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} tax was payable under section 212.1 of the Act and
    the person was not entitled to a rebate of that tax under section
    261.2 of the Act.

- [21]{.lawlabel} Property that is brought into a participating province
  by a person after having been used in, and removed from, a
  participating province by the person and in respect of which the
  person was not entitled to claim a rebate under section 261.1.

- [22]{.lawlabel} Property (other than a specified motor vehicle) that
  is brought into a participating province by a registrant (other than a
  registrant whose net tax is determined under section 225.1 of the Act
  or under Part IV or V of the [Streamlined Accounting (GST/HST)
  Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-91-51)) for consumption, use or
  supply exclusively in the course of commercial activities of the
  registrant.

- [23]{.lawlabel} Prescribed property brought into a participating
  province in prescribed circumstances, subject to such terms and
  conditions as may be prescribed.

- [24]{.lawlabel} A specified motor vehicle that is brought into a
  participating province by a person after having been supplied to the
  person by way of sale in a non-participating province in circumstances
  in which tax was not payable under subsection 165(1) of the Act in
  respect of the supply.

- [25]{.lawlabel} A mobile home or a floating home that has been used or
  occupied in Canada as a place of residence for individuals.

- [26]{.lawlabel} Property referred to in subsection 178.3(1) or
  178.4(1) of the Act where it is brought into a participating province
  by an independent sales contractor (within the meaning of section
  178.1 of the Act) who is not a distributor in respect of whom an
  approval granted under subsection 178.2(4) on application made jointly
  with a direct seller is in effect.

- [27]{.lawlabel} [[[In vitro]{.otherLang lang="la"}
  embryos]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as defined in section 3 of the
  [Assisted Human Reproduction Act](/eng/acts/A-13.4).

## PART II Non-Taxable Property and Services for Purposes of Subdivision B {#part-ii-non-taxable-property-and-services-for-purposes-of-subdivision-b .SchedHeadL1}

(*Subsection 220.08(3)*)

- [1]{.lawlabel} A supply of property or a service to a registrant
  (other than a registrant whose net tax is determined under section
  225.1 of the Act or under Part IV or V of the [Streamlined Accounting
  (GST/HST) Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-91-51)) who is acquiring
  the property or service for consumption, use or supply exclusively in
  the course of commercial activities of the registrant.

- [2]{.lawlabel} A zero-rated supply.

- [3]{.lawlabel} A supply of a service (other than a custodial or
  nominee service in respect of securities or precious metals of the
  person) in respect of tangible personal property that is removed from
  the participating provinces as soon after the service is performed as
  is reasonable having regard to the circumstances surrounding the
  removal and is not consumed, used or supplied in the participating
  provinces after the service is performed and before the removal of the
  property.

- [4]{.lawlabel} A supply of a service rendered in connection with
  criminal, civil or administrative litigation outside the participating
  provinces, other than a service rendered before the commencement of
  such litigation.

- [5]{.lawlabel} A supply of a transportation service.

- [6]{.lawlabel} A supply of a telecommunication service.

- [7]{.lawlabel} A prescribed supply of property or a service where the
  property or service is acquired by the recipient of the supply in
  prescribed circumstances, subject to such terms and conditions as may
  be prescribed.

## RELATED PROVISIONS {#related-provisions .scheduleTitleText}

- --- 2002, c. 22, s. 305

  - Meaning of [[implementation date]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

    [305]{.lawlabel} In sections 306 to 320, [[implementation
    date]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the day on which Parts 3 and 4 come
    into force.

- --- 2002, c. 22, ss. 308 to 311

  - ###### Transitional treatment of excise taxes on wine {#transitional-treatment-of-excise-taxes-on-wine .MarginalNote}

    [308]{.lawlabel} The following rules apply to wine on which tax was
    imposed under section 27 of the [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15) but
    had not become payable before the implementation date :

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} as of that day, the tax is relieved;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} as of that day, Parts III, VI and VII of the
      [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15) cease to apply in respect of the
      wine;

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of imported wine that has not been
      released under the [Customs Act](/eng/acts/C-52.6), this Act, the
      [Customs Act](/eng/acts/C-52.6) and the [Customs
      Tariff](/eng/acts/C-54.011) apply in respect of the wine as though
      it were imported on that day;

    - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of bulk wine to which paragraph (c)
      does not apply, this Act applies in respect of it as though it
      were produced in Canada on that day

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the wine is located in a ferment-on-premises
        facility or at the residence of an individual, by the individual
        who owned the wine immediately before that day, or

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, by the person having
        possession of it immediately before that day; and

    - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in the case of wine to which neither
      paragraph (c) nor (d) apply, this Act applies in respect of it as
      though

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} it were produced and packaged in Canada on that
        day by the person having possession of it immediately before
        that day and the person were permitted under this Act to produce
        and package it, and

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of wine in the possession of a
        duty free shop or an accredited representative or delivered as
        ships' stores in accordance with the [Ships' Stores
        Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-96-40), it had been entered
        into an excise warehouse and then removed from the warehouse in
        accordance with paragraph 147(1)(a) on that day.

- --- 2002, c. 22, ss. 308 to 311

  - ###### Transitional treatment of packaged wine in inventory of small manufacturers {#transitional-treatment-of-packaged-wine-in-inventory-of-small-manufacturers .MarginalNote}

    - [309]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} If tax under Part IV of the
      [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15) is not payable in respect of
      packaged wine because it was produced by a person who is exempt
      from payment of excise tax under the [Small Manufacturers or
      Producers Exemption Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-82-498),
      subsection 135(1) does not apply to the wine if it was packaged
      before the implementation date.

    - ###### Determination of sales for transitional purposes {#determination-of-sales-for-transitional-purposes .MarginalNote}

      [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the period beginning on the implementation
      date and ending on the day that is one year after that day, the
      words "products subject to duty under subsection (1), or would
      have been so subject to duty in the absence of this subsection,"
      in paragraph 135(2)(b) shall be read as "goods referred to in
      paragraph 2(1)(a) of the [Small Manufacturers or Producers
      Exemption Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-82-498)".

- --- 2002, c. 22, ss. 308 to 311

  - ###### Application of Act to tax-paid packaged wine {#application-of-act-to-tax-paid-packaged-wine .MarginalNote}

    - [310]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} If packaged wine on which tax
      imposed under section 27 of the [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15)
      became payable before the implementation date is entered into the
      excise warehouse of an excise warehouse licensee on or before the
      end of six months after that day, this Act applies in respect of
      the wine as though it were produced and packaged in Canada by the
      licensee and the licensee were permitted under this Act to produce
      and package it on the day it is entered into the warehouse.

    - ###### Refund of excise tax paid on packaged wine {#refund-of-excise-tax-paid-on-packaged-wine .MarginalNote}

      [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the tax imposed under section 27 of the
      [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15) in respect of the wine entered
      into the warehouse has been paid, the licensee may apply to the
      Minister for a refund of the tax.

    - ###### Limitation {#limitation .MarginalNote}

      [(3)]{.lawlabel} No refund shall be paid under this section unless
      the application for the refund is filed with the Minister in the
      prescribed form and manner within one year after the
      implementation date.

- --- 2002, c. 22, ss. 308 to 311

  - ###### Application of Act to tax-paid bulk wine {#application-of-act-to-tax-paid-bulk-wine .MarginalNote}

    - [311]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} If bulk wine on which tax
      imposed under section 27 of the [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15)
      became payable before the implementation date is entered into the
      specified premises of a licensed user on that day, this Act
      applies in respect of the wine as though it were produced in
      Canada on that day by the user and the user were permitted to
      produce the wine.

    - ###### Refund of excise tax paid on bulk wine {#refund-of-excise-tax-paid-on-bulk-wine .MarginalNote}

      [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the tax imposed under section 27 of the
      [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15) in respect of the wine entered
      into the specified premises of a licensed user has been paid, the
      user may apply to the Minister for a refund of the tax.

    - ###### Limitation {#limitation-1 .MarginalNote}

      [(3)]{.lawlabel} No refund shall be paid under this section unless
      the application for the refund is filed with the Minister in the
      prescribed form and manner within one year after the
      implementation date.

- --- 2002, c. 22, s. 314

  - ###### Application of Act to alcohol in bottle-your-own premises {#application-of-act-to-alcohol-in-bottle-your-own-premises .MarginalNote}

    [314]{.lawlabel} The following rules apply to alcohol contained in a
    special container located on a person's bottle-your-own premises on
    the implementation date :

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person shall, despite subsections 78(1) and
      83(1), mark the container on that day;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of spirits, this Act applies in
      respect of them as though the duty, at a rate determined by the
      application of section 1 of Part I of the schedule to the [Excise
      Act](/eng/acts/E-14), that had become payable before that day in
      respect of them were imposed and, if the duty is paid, paid under
      this Act; and

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of wine,

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} for the purposes of subsection 135(1), section
        82 does not apply to the marking of the container under
        paragraph (a), and

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} this Act applies in respect of the wine as
        though the tax under section 27 of the [Excise Tax
        Act](/eng/acts/E-15) that had become payable before that day in
        respect of it were a duty that was imposed and, if the tax is
        paid, paid under this Act.

- --- 2002, c. 22, ss. 316, 317

  - ###### Transitional treatment of Canadian manufactured tobacco products {#transitional-treatment-of-canadian-manufactured-tobacco-products .MarginalNote}

    - [316]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} The following rules apply to a
      tobacco product manufactured in Canada before the implementation
      date :

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if tax on the product imposed under section 23
        of the [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15) had not become payable
        before that day,

        - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the tax is relieved,

        - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if duty on the product imposed under the
          [Excise Act](/eng/acts/E-14) had not become payable before
          that day, the duty is relieved, and

        - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} this Act applies in respect of the product
          as though it were manufactured in Canada on that day by the
          manufacturer to the same extent that the product was
          manufactured immediately before that day;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the product was stamped or marked under the
        [Excise Act](/eng/acts/E-14), the product is deemed to be
        stamped or marked, as the case may be, under this Act; and

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the [Excise Act](/eng/acts/E-14) and Parts III,
        VI and VII of the [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15) cease to
        apply in respect of the product.

    - ###### Refund of duty paid {#refund-of-duty-paid .MarginalNote}

      [(2)]{.lawlabel} If duty imposed under the [Excise
      Act](/eng/acts/E-14) on a tobacco product manufactured in Canada
      before the implementation date had become payable before that day
      but tax under section 23 of the [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15)
      had not become payable before that day, the manufacturer of the
      product may apply to the Minister for a refund of the duty.

    - ###### Limitation {#limitation-2 .MarginalNote}

      [(3)]{.lawlabel} No refund shall be paid under this section unless
      the application for the refund is filed with the Minister in the
      prescribed form and manner within one year after the
      implementation date.

- --- 2002, c. 22, ss. 316, 317

  - ###### Transitional treatment of imported tobacco products {#transitional-treatment-of-imported-tobacco-products .MarginalNote}

    [317]{.lawlabel} The following rules apply to an imported tobacco
    product :

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if duty levied under section 21 of the [Customs
      Tariff](/eng/acts/C-54.011) and tax imposed under section 23 of
      the [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15) on the product had not become
      payable before the implementation date,

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the duty and tax are relieved, and

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} this Act and the [Customs
        Act](/eng/acts/C-52.6) apply in respect of the product as though
        it were imported into Canada on that day by the importer;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the product was stamped or marked under the
      [Excise Act](/eng/acts/E-14), the product is deemed to be stamped
      or marked, as the case may be, under this Act; and

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the [Excise Act](/eng/acts/E-14) and Parts III,
      VI and VII of the [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15) cease to apply
      in respect of the product.

- --- 2003, c. 15, s. 59

  - [59]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of applying the provisions of the
    [Customs Act](/eng/acts/C-52.6) and the [Excise Tax
    Act](/eng/acts/E-15) that provide for the payment of, or the
    liability to pay, interest in respect of any amount, the amount
    shall be determined and interest shall be computed on it as though
    this Act had been assented to on June 18, 2002.

- --- 2012, c. 31, s. 96

  - [96]{.lawlabel} The Input Tax Credit Allocation Methods (GST/HST)
    Regulations are deemed

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to have been made under section 277 of the
      [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15);

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for the purposes of subsection 5(1) of the
      [Statutory Instruments Act](/eng/acts/S-22), to have been
      transmitted to the Clerk of the Privy Council for registration;
      and

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} to have met the publication requirements of
      subsection 11(1) of the [Statutory Instruments
      Act](/eng/acts/S-22).

- --- 2016, c. 12, s. 94

  - ###### Paragraph 150(2)(b) --- election in effect on March 22, 2016 {#paragraph-1502b-election-in-effect-on-march-22-2016 .MarginalNote}

    [94]{.lawlabel} If a supply is made between a person and a
    corporation that have jointly made an election under subsection
    150(1) of the [Excise Tax Act](/eng/acts/E-15), if the election is
    in effect on March 22, 2016 and on the day on which the agreement
    for the supply is entered into and if the agreement is entered into
    after March 22, 2016 but before March 22, 2017, then paragraph
    150(2)(b) of that Act is to be read as follows in respect of the
    supply:

    > ::: ReadAsText
    > - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an [[imported taxable
    >   supply]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, as defined in section 217;
    >
    > - [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} a supply made between a person and a
    >   corporation if
    >
    >   - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the supply is
    >
    >     - [(A)]{.lawlabel} a supply of a service and it is not the
    >       case that all or substantially all of the service will be
    >       performed before March 22, 2017, or
    >
    >     - [(B)]{.lawlabel} a supply of property by way of lease,
    >       licence or similar arrangement and it is not the case that
    >       all or substantially all of the property will be delivered
    >       or made available to the recipient of the supply before
    >       March 22, 2017, and
    >
    >   - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the person and the corporation
    >
    >     - [(A)]{.lawlabel} are not members of the same closely related
    >       group at any time after the day on which the agreement for
    >       the supply is entered into but before March 22, 2017, or
    >
    >     - [(B)]{.lawlabel} are not members of the same closely related
    >       group on March 22, 2017; or
    > :::

- --- 2023, c. 26, s. 114(6)

  - - []{.lawlabel} [(6)]{.lawlabel} Despite section 298 of the Act, the
      Minister of National Revenue may assess, reassess or make an
      additional assessment of any amount in respect of paragraph (r.6)
      of the definition [[financial service]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} in
      subsection 123(1) of the Act, as amended by subsection (1), at any
      time on or before the later of the day that is one year after the
      day on which the legislation enacting subsection (1) receives
      royal assent and the last day of the period otherwise allowed
      under that section for making the assessment, reassessment or
      additional assessment.
